topic: which model produces the renewal-risk scores shown to account managers

options.B: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

versions.option_text: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

chain.speaker: Diego
chain.gist: Diego proposes shipping the gradient-boosted model for the renewal-risk scores that account managers see from next quarter.

chain.speaker: Diego
chain.gist: Diego argues that on the holdout from the last four quarters it catches 71 percent of the accounts that later churned in the top risk decile, against 52 percent for the logistic baseline.

chain.speaker: Henrik
chain.gist: Henrik agrees without naming the model, by telling Rohan to set up the weekly scoring job.

chain.speaker: Chloe
chain.gist: Chloe reports an audit finding that 18 percent of the holdout accounts also appear in the training data under a renamed customer ID after a CRM merge, so the 71 percent is inflated.

chain.speaker: Elif
chain.gist: Elif objects that the headline gain cannot be trusted and that account managers would be shown scores nobody can explain.

chain.speaker: Elif
chain.gist: Elif argues for the logistic regression: on the deduplicated holdout the gradient-boosted model catches 64 percent and the logistic one 61 percent, and the logistic coefficients can be read out to account managers.
chain.option: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

chain.speaker: Henrik
chain.gist: Henrik decides to ship the logistic regression model instead.
chain.option: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

chain.speaker: Rohan
chain.gist: Rohan reports that the logistic model says 12 percent risk for enterprise accounts where observed churn last quarter was 31 percent, across 40 enterprise accounts.
chain.option: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

chain.speaker: Diego
chain.gist: Diego objects that the logistic model is underrating enterprise accounts, which hold 58 percent of renewal revenue.
chain.option: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

chain.speaker: Henrik
chain.gist: Henrik reopens the model decision after Chloe confirms the enterprise gap holds on a second quarter of data.
chain.option: the logistic regression model with readable coefficients

chain.speaker: Diego
chain.gist: Diego argues for going back to the gradient-boosted model because, recalibrated on the deduplicated data, it matches enterprise churn within 4 points, and per-account reason codes now cover the explanation concern.

chain.speaker: Henrik
chain.gist: Henrik decides to ship the gradient-boosted model with the reason codes.
